Decide the shared concept yourself from the stated facts, rather than taking an existing category code as its meaning. Give a precise definition supported by the descriptions; do not merely rename an existing category or invent missing facts.”

Model output (not verified)

Name proposed by the model:
Damaged object repaired and kept in use

An item matches when its own description states that an existing object that is damaged, such as bent, torn, broken or leaking, is repaired, mended, straightened, sealed or otherwise fixed. The description must also state that the same object is kept, remains in use or is used again. Both conditions need affirmative text in the item's own description. Making a new object, even from leftover material, is not a repair of an existing object. A description that states the damaged object is discarded or replaced by a different object makes the keep condition false. When the description does not say whether either condition holds, membership is unknown.

Reason that the model gave: Three captions describe the same pattern across different existing codes. Item 41001 states that a bent bookmark is straightened and that the existing piece is kept. Item 41002 states that a torn satchel is mended and that the same bag is kept. Item 41003 states that a leaking jug is sealed and that the same jug remains in use. This concept crosses codes K1, K2 and K3, so it is not a renamed existing category. Other captions do not show both conditions as stated. Item 41004 states the broken organizer is put in recycling and a new one is unpacked, so its text states the object is not kept. Items 41005 and 41006 describe making a new tray and a new knob, not repair of an existing damaged object. Item 41007 states that no completed activity is described, and item 41008 states the subject is not described. This proposal does not classify the pool; a reviewer must confirm membership.

Quotations that the model cited: item 41001, description: “A bent metal bookmark is straightened with pliers and used again. The existing piece is kept.”. The caption states that a bent bookmark, which is a damaged existing object, is straightened, which is a fix. It also states that it is used again and that the existing piece is kept, which meets the keep condition. item 41002, description: “A torn canvas satchel is mended with a needle and spare thread so it can carry books again. The same bag is kept.”. The caption states that a torn satchel, which is a damaged existing object, is mended, which is a fix. It states that the same bag is kept, which meets the keep condition. The phrase about carrying books gives a purpose only and does not establish that the bag actually carried books; the definition does not need that. item 41003, description: “A leaking clay jug is sealed and returned to watering plants. The same jug remains in use.”. The caption states that a leaking jug, which is a damaged existing object, is sealed, which is a fix. It states that the same jug remains in use, which meets the keep condition.
